purpose: Quantify whether the apparent Maasvlakte 2 mismatch can plausibly arise from Natural Earth 1:10m generalization rather than treating it as a verified reclamation omission.

rotterdamStudySegment.interpretation: The prior point-to-boundary distance is of the same order as the generalized source segment lengths and therefore cannot by itself prove a missing reclamation footprint.

findings: Pando/Natural Earth preserves Netherlands aggregate land-plus-inland-water area surprisingly closely while using far fewer vertices.
Local coastline displacement at max zoom can be large even when national aggregate area is close.
The country polygon semantically includes substantial inland water; point-in-country is not a dry-land classifier.

Subtracting all relevant inland-water geometry would move the footprint toward actual dry-land area, but the current Natural Earth lakes layer is incomplete/generalized and contains only two intersecting named lake features in the Netherlands study bbox.
Maasvlakte 2 remains unclassified at footprint level until current TOP10NL/PDOK coastline coordinates are directly compared with the Natural Earth line.
